slides.title: A new study
slides.body: The Rift Valley Institute interviewed 47 people in Kaffa, Bench-Sheko and Sheka zones of the southwest, The Reporter says.

slides.title: What it alleges
slides.body: Politically connected traders benefit from selective enforcement, and some officials both regulate the trade and invest in it. Not independently verified.

slides.title: Farmers under pressure
slides.body: Smallholders rely on trader loans, the study says some communities lost land to investment licences, and new EU traceability rules could add costs.

slides.title: Fair rules. Support for farmers.
slides.body: Follow for sourced updates from across Ethiopia.
